facts.label: Gaps
facts.text: Adjusted EBITDA and the issuer's net leverage appear only in the three earnings releases, which are unaudited; neither annual report nor any quarterly report prints either term. The release defines net debt as total corporate debt excluding the GSE warehouse facilities, net of cash or liquidity, and net leverage as that net debt over trailing twelve-month adjusted EBITDA. The issuer's net leverage therefore rests on corporate debt only and on adjusted EBITDA, so it will not agree with a ratio built on reported EBITDA or on debt that includes the warehouse lines, and each ratio must be labelled; whether the warehouse lines count as debt is a perimeter decision for the Financial foundation, not a source question. Reported EBITDA has to be built from statement lines. The issuer's net leverage therefore rests on corporate debt only and on adjusted EBITDA, so it will not agree with a ratio built on reported EBITDA or on debt that includes the warehouse lines, and each ratio must be labelled; whether the warehouse lines count as debt is a perimeter decision for the Financial foundation, not a source question. Reported EBITDA has to be built from statement lines. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 28; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 34

The third-quarter release and the third-quarter quarterly report disagree on the nine-month 2026 cash-flow totals: the quarterly report prints operating cash flow of USD (175.4) million against USD (171.3) million in the release, investing of USD (198.6) million against USD (201.1) million, and financing of USD 381.9 million against USD 380.2 million, while both print the same net increase in cash. The differences net to zero, which is consistent with a classification difference, but neither document says why the totals differ; the release says only that other reclassifications may have been made to conform presentation. The quarterly report controls under the source hierarchy and the release figures stay beside it. The first and second quarter releases agree with their quarterly reports on operating cash flow. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 15; EX-99.1_2026-04-30_nmrkex991043026-secversion.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-03-31_nmrk-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 23; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_nmrkex991-secversion.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_nmrk-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5

A stand-alone third-quarter 2025 report and a fourth-quarter 2025 results release were not supplied. The third-quarter 2025 figures are available as comparatives inside the third-quarter 2026 report, and the fourth quarter of 2025 can be derived only as the 2025 annual figure less the nine-month 2025 comparative. A derived quarter or trailing twelve-month figure is valid only when every component is printed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 173–174

Directors, executive officers, executive compensation, beneficial ownership and related transactions in the 2025 annual report are incorporated by reference to an amendment to the annual report or a 2026 proxy statement, neither of which was supplied. Business & governance can describe control by Cantor and the voting arrangements from the notes and risk factors but cannot describe the board or management from a primary document. Supply the proxy statement or annual report amendment to close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 264

Two terms differ between the 2025 annual report and the later quarterly reports because the later reports describe later events: the issuer-stated ratings, where the S&P and JCR ratings differ between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30, and the revolving credit facility's size and maturity, which the annual report describes as it stood before the amendment and restatement reported in the second quarter. The later report controls each current term. No rating agency report or rating action was supplied, so the ratings rest on the issuer's own statements. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 147

No bond or loan prices, deal terms, peer set, valuation inputs, portfolio file, management bridge or research question was supplied; the run settings leave these blank, not at zero. Peer benchmark, Market-implied risk, Security selection and Committee decision would have nothing to work from if they were requested, and the first run of this pathway has no earlier run for a comparison.

The supplied files are text only. Tables are flattened into lines, charts and diagrams are not carried as images, and a page in a citation is a chunk of the extraction rather than a printed page of the filing. The original HTML hash stated on the first page of each text file is recorded in the input inventory for provenance. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1

facts.text: Corporate debt at carrying value rose from USD 671.746 million at year-end 2025 to USD 877.508 million at 2026-09-30 as the revolver draw went from USD 75.000 million to USD 280.000 million, while cash moved from USD 229.109 million to USD 239.983 million, so net debt rose by USD 194.888 million to USD 637.525 million. Net debt over last-twelve-month reported EBITDA moved from 1.07x at year-end 2025 to 1.38x, still below 1.40x at year-end 2024, because last-twelve-month reported EBITDA grew from USD 415.305 million to USD 460.319 million. The senior notes principal of USD 600.000 million is unchanged and matures in 2029, and the revolver now matures in 2030, so the added debt sits in the instrument with the later maturity. facts.text: The strongest contrary evidence is the issuer's own framing: on adjusted EBITDA net debt is 1.00x, because the adjusted measure adds back USD 196.892 million of equity-based compensation and partner allocations and removes USD 92.456 million of non-cash servicing-right gains in the nine months. facts.label: Cash flow quality
facts.text: Operating cash flow as reported was USD (175.421) million in the nine months because loan originations exceeded loan sales by USD 414.611 million in the period; excluding loan activity it was USD 239.190 million against USD 146.700 million a year earlier, and after purchases of fixed assets of USD 47.203 million the free cash flow excluding loan activity was USD 191.987 million against USD 127.022 million. Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

Reported EBITDA is derived, not stated: none of the five periodic reports prints EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA, so every reported-basis ratio rests on a definition chosen here (income before taxes and noncontrolling interests plus net interest plus depreciation and amortization). The issuer-adjusted measure is larger by USD 136.873 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, which moves net leverage from 1.38x to 1.00x. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the issuer's reconciliation by period in a filing or state the definition choice in the credit assessment. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C8

Adjusted EBITDA for FY2024 is not supplied, so the three adjusted ratios for FY2024 are not calculable, and FY2025 adjusted EBITDA is stated only as USD 562.4 million, rounded to one decimal. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the FY2024 and FY2025 fourth-quarter releases. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 8

The third-quarter release and the quarterly report differ on nine-month 2026 operating cash flow (USD (171.272) million against USD (175.421) million), investing and financing; the net change agrees. The quarterly report is used. Severity: Low. Action: ask the issuer for the reclassification. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C39

Cash interest paid includes interest on the warehouse facilities and cannot be split for twelve months; corporate debt interest is available only for the nine months (USD 45.734 million). Cover is therefore conservative for corporate debt. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the corporate interest line for the full year. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 61–62; calculation C30

Cells the filings print as a dash, and cash-flow lines that a filing does not print for a period, are shown as not supplied, not as zero; they sit in lines of the cash flow and balance sheet tables such as acquisitions, treasury stock repurchases and related-party receivables. No total depends on them. Severity: Low. Action: none needed for totals. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 176–177

The FY2025 annual report recasts one FY2024 operating cash-flow line (Other, USD (1.110) million against USD (1.078) million in the FY2024 report) while every total agrees. The later comparative is used. Severity: Low. Action: none. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_nmrk-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 172–174; 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 176–177

Borrowing of USD 28.000 million under the Multifamily Bridge repurchase agreement is carried within accounts payable, accrued expenses and other liabilities and is not in Total Debt; the agreement is secured by loans held for investment. Severity: Low. Action: the credit assessment should weigh it with the warehouse funding. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 114

Right-of-use liabilities of USD 426.626 million and the financial guarantee liability for the Fannie Mae loss-sharing program are outside Total Debt and are not quantified as leverage here. Severity: Low. Action: the credit assessment should weigh them as claims outside debt. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 62–64

Maintenance and growth capital expenditure are not disclosed, only purchases of fixed assets, so no maintenance-only cash-flow measure is calculated. Severity: Low. Action: none available from the filings. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23

No discrete fourth-quarter 2025 or stand-alone quarters were constructed; last twelve months are built from year-to-date stubs, which is valid because every component is printed. Severity: Low. Action: none. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 174

The dividend row in the post-balance-sheet table uses the cover-page share count of 2026-11-03, not the record-date count, so its amount and pro forma figures are estimates. Severity: Low. Action: replace with the record-date count when disclosed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 92; calculation C36; calculation C37

No covenant level or reported covenant figure is printed, so covenant headroom is not calculable and no test of the revolver's availability is possible. Severity: Low for this module. Action: obtain the executed credit agreement. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62

The legal rank of the warehouse facilities against the senior notes and revolver is not stated by any source, so they are left out of the debt stack; the company reports one segment, so no segment schedule beyond service-line revenue is possible. Severity: Low. Action: none. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 59–60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 92

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Control sits with one family through Cantor and is larger than its economic interest, which makes the board and borrowing decisions subject to one group's preferences. Class B shares carry ten votes each, and as of 2026-09-30 Mr. Brandon Lutnick beneficially controlled 58.6% of the vote, while Cantor Fitzgerald, L.P. holds 11.7% of the economics and 56.5% of the voting power and CFGM, Cantor's managing general partner, holds 0.8% of the economics and 1.2% of the voting power. The stated protection for other holders is Audit Committee approval of matters that need it, and a Lutnick family voting agreement that directs the family's votes, so control is stable rather than contestable. Newmark is a controlled company under Nasdaq rules and could opt out of the majority-independent-board requirement, which it has not done to date. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a governance concern is procedural and structural, and the company states that it has not relied on any controlled-company exemption from Nasdaq governance standards to date. Related-party transactions need Audit Committee approval and the authorizations state arm's-length price terms, the former executive chairman completed the divestiture of his holdings and holds no voting or dispositive power, revenues are spread over three service lines and many clients, and the quarterly report shows no outstanding balance under the Cantor credit agreement. The view would turn more positive if the proxy materials show a majority of independent directors and an independent chair, if the issuer names a chief executive successor with an orderly handover, and if insider repurchases stop; it would turn more negative if Cantor sold its notes at a discount or the revolver were drawn to fund further insider buybacks. The Board has also had a leadership advisory firm assisting with long-term succession planning since July 2025, which lowers the risk that the end-2026 transition is unplanned. A single Class B voting block can also be an asset to creditors if it is a stable, long-horizon holder, which the sources neither confirm nor rule out. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence for a better view is momentum, modest leverage and improving ratings: nine-month revenue grew 18.36%, third-quarter revenue grew 12.71%, last-twelve-month reported EBITDA is 10.84% above FY2025, net leverage on the issuer's own adjusted measure is 1.00x, S&P raised the rating to BBB- on 2026-09-16, and management still expects its best-ever full year. The profile would improve if shareholder returns fell back inside free cash flow and the revolver were repaid, if a chief executive successor were named with an orderly handover, and if the executed credit agreement showed ample covenant headroom. It would weaken if capital markets revenue fell again year on year in the fourth quarter, if net leverage stayed above the FY2024 level of 1.40x after the dividend, if revolver availability fell toward the USD 365 million of 2026-03-31, or if a downgrade triggered the rate increase on the notes. facts.text: Cash conversion is high and capital intensity low. facts.label: Market forces and external factors
facts.text: Competitive rivalry is the force that matters most to margins and market position. The annual report describes an industry that is fragmented and competitive, names larger rivals such as CBRE, Jones Lang LaSalle and Cushman & Wakefield, and says some competitors are substantially larger than Newmark; the third-quarter report says Newmark believes it gained share in investment sales, yet its U.S. debt volumes fell about 37% while industry originations rose, which the issuer ties to a strong prior-year comparison. Buyer power is limited by client spread, with the top ten clients at 9.1% of FY2025 revenue and clients increasingly awarding work to full-service firms. Supplier power sits with producers, who earn a substantial portion or all of their pay from production and are retained with advances, so producer departures are a margin and revenue risk. The documents do not discuss new entrants or substitutes, so those forces are not established. facts.label: Market forces and external factors
facts.text: The external factors that move credit are economic and regulatory. A ten-year Treasury yield up about 113 bp in the quarter to 5.3%, tied by the issuer to the Middle East conflict and energy prices, raises financing costs and rate volatility for property buyers and offsets the help from narrow credit spreads. Agency programs add a regulatory layer: capital and liquidity requirements for Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac lending include the net worth test the issuer calls its most restrictive, and the Fannie Mae loss-sharing exposure rises with agency loan performance. Technology cuts both ways, because artificial intelligence firms drive office leasing demand while the annual report lists their use as a risk. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is long-term rates that stay near 5.3% through the year-end selling season, so closings slip and the fourth quarter lands at the low end of the revised outlook, which implies fourth-quarter revenue growth of -1.40%. The first operational break is in the transaction lines, leasing and capital markets, while servicing and management fees keep growing. Compensation flexes with commissions, but depreciation, lease costs and cash interest do not, so reported EBITDA falls faster than revenue. As a severity marker chosen by the analyst, not a forecast, take reported EBITDA back at its FY2024 level: net debt at 2026-09-30 would then be 1.89x EBITDA, or 1.92x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-10-28, and interest cover would be 5.98x. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: Liquidity holds in this case. USD 620 million of the revolver is undrawn and no corporate debt matures before 2029, so no refinancing event arises within the scenario. Management has levers: share repurchases and the dividend are discretionary with USD 189.5 million of repurchase authorization still unused, purchases of fixed assets are only 1.53% of revenue, and producer pay flexes. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress; the first constraint would be leverage at 1.89x to 1.92x and the investment-grade ratings, where a downgrade lifts the notes rate, and not cash. The scenario would break this view only if repurchases continued at the nine-month pace while earnings fell. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Newmark presents an adequate business profile supported by revenue spread across three service lines, low capital intensity and investment-grade ratings at Fitch and S&P, but credit quality is constrained by capital returns above free cash flow, controlling-holder influence and an earnings base that depends on deal closings in the fourth quarter. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow excluding loan activity converted 72.52% of last-twelve-month reported EBITDA and about two-fifths of revenue is recurring. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on keeping the BBB- ratings and on the notes due 2029 being refinanced before they become current. The primary downside path is a weak fourth quarter and a downgrade while the revolver funds distributions. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indenture, the proxy statement, and peer and market data. Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: shareholder returns funded by the revolver ahead of a deal-dependent fourth quarter. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 116; calculation C51; calculation C30; calculation C55

## Findings
### Bottom line

The eight supplied filings and releases are enough to run business, financial and fundamental credit work on Newmark, but they cannot support any view on covenant headroom, security terms or relative value.

The newest quarterly report was signed 12 days before the cutoff, and the 2024 and 2025 annual reports are audited. Two points limit the financial work: adjusted EBITDA and the issuer's net leverage appear only in the unaudited earnings releases, and the third-quarter release and quarterly report print different nine-month 2026 cash-flow totals, so the filing controls under the source hierarchy and the release figure stays beside it. No executed credit agreement or indenture was supplied, and the filings state covenant compliance without printing any covenant level, so creditor protection can be read only as management describes it.

## Gaps

The executed debt documents were not supplied, and the run settings declare none. The annual report's exhibit index lists the indenture, the second supplemental indenture, the form of the 2029 notes and the earlier credit agreements, and the second quarter report's exhibit index lists the current third amended and restated credit agreement, all by reference only. Covenant definitions, guarantor terms, baskets and events of default therefore cannot be read from a primary document. The gap is minor for the requested modules, which can work from the filings' own debt notes, and blocking for Legal & covenants and Covenant capacity, which this run does not request. To close it, supply the executed credit agreement, the indenture and the supplemental indenture.

No covenant level, test result or headroom figure is printed anywhere in the supplied sources, after a search of every file for covenant, leverage, coverage and net worth terms. The quarterly and annual reports state only that Newmark was in compliance with all financial covenants at the balance-sheet dates, and the 2025 annual report names minimum interest coverage and maximum leverage tests only for the former delayed draw term loan, which it describes as consistent with the credit facility then in place. The annual report also names GSE and HUD eligibility criteria, including minimum net worth and operational liquidity, without printing their levels. Headroom is not calculable, and Fundamental credit can report management's compliance statement only; inferring levels from the issuer's net leverage figure would be unsupported.

Adjusted EBITDA and the issuer's net leverage appear only in the three earnings releases, which are unaudited; neither annual report nor any quarterly report prints either term. The release defines net debt as total corporate debt excluding the GSE warehouse facilities, net of cash or liquidity, and net leverage as that net debt over trailing twelve-month adjusted EBITDA. The issuer's net leverage therefore rests on corporate debt only and on adjusted EBITDA, so it will not agree with a ratio built on reported EBITDA or on debt that includes the warehouse lines, and each ratio must be labelled; whether the warehouse lines count as debt is a perimeter decision for the Financial foundation, not a source question. Reported EBITDA has to be built from statement lines.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Newmark's corporate debt is moderate against reported earnings, with net leverage of 1.38x on reported EBITDA and 1.00x on the issuer's adjusted figure, so the reported measure is the prudent basis for sizing credit risk.

Interest cover on reported EBITDA is 8.17x, undrawn revolver capacity is USD 620.0 million, and the nearest corporate maturity is 2029. Reported EBITDA is derived because the filings state none, and it is far below the issuer's adjusted measure because it carries equity-based compensation as a cost and counts non-cash servicing-right gains as revenue. The third-quarter release and quarterly report print different nine-month cash-flow totals, so the quarterly report is used. The warehouse facilities are excluded from debt as matched funding of loans held for sale; with them, total debt would be much higher.

### Leverage and coverage

Corporate debt at carrying value rose from USD 671.746 million at year-end 2025 to USD 877.508 million at 2026-09-30 as the revolver draw went from USD 75.000 million to USD 280.000 million, while cash moved from USD 229.109 million to USD 239.983 million, so net debt rose by USD 194.888 million to USD 637.525 million. Over the same nine months the group spent USD 210.528 million on share repurchases and USD 72.100 million on convertible debt and other contract assets, which is consistent with the extra debt funding capital return and investment. Net debt over last-twelve-month reported EBITDA moved from 1.07x at year-end 2025 to 1.38x, still below 1.40x at year-end 2024, because last-twelve-month reported EBITDA grew from USD 415.305 million to USD 460.319 million. The senior notes principal of USD 600.000 million is unchanged and matures in 2029, and the revolver now matures in 2030, so the added debt sits in the instrument with the later maturity.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 173–174; calculation C19; calculation C22; calculation C40; calculation C11

The strongest contrary evidence is the issuer's own framing: on adjusted EBITDA net debt is 1.00x, because the adjusted measure adds back USD 196.892 million of equity-based compensation and partner allocations and removes USD 92.456 million of non-cash servicing-right gains in the nine months. Reported EBITDA treats the compensation as a cost, which is the conservative reading for creditors because the group also spent cash on repurchases and partner distributions of USD 29.209 million in the same period. The view would change if the issuer disclosed how much of the equity-based charge is settled in shares, which would move the right denominator toward the adjusted figure.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C38

Interest cover on reported EBITDA is 8.17x for the last twelve months against 10.50x in FY2024. Cash interest paid rose between FY2024 and FY2025 from USD 32.129 million to USD 56.368 million, and part of it is not corporate-debt interest: corporate debt interest and issue-cost amortization were USD 45.734 million of the USD 53.779 million paid in the nine months, and the sources do not itemise the other USD 8.045 million, which may include warehouse facility interest. Cover on corporate debt alone is therefore better than the printed ratio but cannot be isolated for twelve months from the sources.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 61–62; 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 178; calculation C14; calculation C30; calculation C31
### Cash flow quality

Operating cash flow as reported was USD (175.421) million in the nine months because loan originations exceeded loan sales by USD 414.611 million in the period; excluding loan activity it was USD 239.190 million against USD 146.700 million a year earlier, and after purchases of fixed assets of USD 47.203 million the free cash flow excluding loan activity was USD 191.987 million against USD 127.022 million. The loans held for sale are funded almost wholly by the warehouse facilities (99.02% at 2026-09-30), so the swing is timing in a matched-funding book, and advances to employees and partners of USD 111.945 million in the nine months recur in every period shown and are the main recurring use of operating cash.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 114–115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 176–177; calculation C32; calculation C33; calculation C34; calculation C35; calculation C29
### Liquidity and maturities

Liquidity at 2026-09-30 is cash of USD 239.983 million plus USD 620.000 million of undrawn revolver, USD 859.983 million in all, against corporate maturities of USD 600.000 million in 2029 and USD 280.000 million in 2030 and no corporate maturity printed before 2029. Restricted cash and short-term investments of USD 131.263 million are not counted. The revolver carries financial covenants whose levels the filings do not print, so headroom cannot be tested and liquidity is shown as stated by the issuer. The warehouse lines renew annually, and the line that was due on 2026-10-03 was renewed after the quarter end to 2027-10-02.

### Definitions and data quality

Three definition choices drive the numbers: reported EBITDA is derived from statement lines because the filings state none, Total Debt is corporate debt only, and the quarterly report is preferred to the third-quarter release where the nine-month cash-flow totals differ. Each is logged in the definition register with its size. Claims outside Total Debt are the warehouse and repurchase funding, USD 28.000 million of borrowing carried within other liabilities, right-of-use liabilities of USD 426.626 million and the Fannie Mae loss-sharing guarantee liability, all of which the credit assessment should weigh separately.

# Business and governance for Newmark Group, Inc.
## Request

Business and governance for Newmark Group, Inc. (issuer nmrk-1690680), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business and operating model, ownership and control, governance, related-party dealing, capital allocation and debt transactions from the supplied annual report, quarterly report and earnings release. Source readiness is supplied; no proxy statement, executed debt document or market data is in scope.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Newmark's business is diversified across service lines and clients, so creditors' main exposure is governance: a Cantor-controlled owner group with 58.6% of the vote, heavy related-party dealing and a chief executive transition at the end of 2026.

The largest service line is 39.57% of nine-month 2026 revenue and the top ten clients were 9.1% of FY2025 revenue, so a single client or line is unlikely to impair debt service. The risks that matter to a bondholder come from the controlling holder: Cantor holds USD 125.0 million of the USD 600.0 million senior notes, 98.48% of the shares repurchased in the third quarter came from the chief executive and his foundation, and the Audit Committee is the stated check on related-party deals. The chief executive is contracted as chief executive only through 2026-12-31, and the sources name no successor.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 133; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 70–71; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C4; calculation C13; calculation C16; calculation C17
### Key findings

Control sits with one family through Cantor and is larger than its economic interest, which makes the board and borrowing decisions subject to one group's preferences. Class B shares carry ten votes each, and as of 2026-09-30 Mr. Brandon Lutnick beneficially controlled 58.6% of the vote, while Cantor Fitzgerald, L.P. holds 11.7% of the economics and 56.5% of the voting power and CFGM, Cantor's managing general partner, holds 0.8% of the economics and 1.2% of the voting power. The stated protection for other holders is Audit Committee approval of matters that need it, and a Lutnick family voting agreement that directs the family's votes, so control is stable rather than contestable. Newmark is a controlled company under Nasdaq rules and could opt out of the majority-independent-board requirement, which it has not done to date.

Related-party dealing with Cantor is extensive and touches creditors directly, because Cantor is both the controlling holder and a lender and service provider. Cantor holds USD 125.0 million of the USD 600.0 million of senior notes due 2029, which is 20.83% of the issue, and its affiliate CF&Co acts as placement agent and makes a market in the notes; Cantor also supplies administrative services, can borrow from and lend to Newmark under a credit agreement of up to USD 250.0 million with no balance outstanding, and is owed a tax receivable liability. These arrangements are approved by the Audit Committee on terms stated to be no less favorable than third parties, but the agreements themselves were not supplied.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 84; calculation C13

Capital returns are heavy and tilted toward insiders, so shareholder distributions are competing with creditors for the same cash. In the third quarter 98.48% of the shares repurchased were bought from the chief executive and his foundation, the quarterly dividend is USD 0.06 per share against USD 0.03 a year earlier, and the repurchase authorization was raised to USD 400.0 million of which USD 189.5 million remained at 2026-09-30. The repurchases were approved by the Audit and Compensation Committees and paid for while the revolver drawings rose, which is the pattern a bondholder should watch.

Leadership continuity is the near-term governance risk: the chief executive is contracted as chief executive only through 2026-12-31, after which he becomes Chairman of the operating subsidiary Newmark & Co., and the sources name no successor; the Board retained a leadership advisory firm in July 2025 and says it is assessing long-term options, so a process exists but its outcome is not disclosed. The Board chair is also the chief legal officer, a director is the son of the former executive chairman and now Chief Strategy Officer, and a Chief Operating Officer was appointed in 2025, so management depth exists but the outcome of the succession process is not disclosed.

The operating model is diversified and part recurring, which is the main offset to governance risk. Management services and servicing is the largest line at 39.57% of nine-month 2026 revenue and grew 19.00%, leasing grew 21.38% and capital markets 14.55%, and the top ten clients were 9.1% of FY2025 revenue; management states a goal of more than USD 2 billion of annual management and servicing revenue by 2029, which is management language, not a forecast.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C4; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C12

Acquisitions are small and cash funded, so they add little integration or leverage risk. The four acquisitions completed in 2026 cost USD 34.6 million in cash in total, against contingent cash consideration of USD 12.2 million recorded for acquisitions since 2022.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 91; calculation C18
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a governance concern is procedural and structural, and the company states that it has not relied on any controlled-company exemption from Nasdaq governance standards to date. Related-party transactions need Audit Committee approval and the authorizations state arm's-length price terms, the former executive chairman completed the divestiture of his holdings and holds no voting or dispositive power, revenues are spread over three service lines and many clients, and the quarterly report shows no outstanding balance under the Cantor credit agreement. The view would turn more positive if the proxy materials show a majority of independent directors and an independent chair, if the issuer names a chief executive successor with an orderly handover, and if insider repurchases stop; it would turn more negative if Cantor sold its notes at a discount or the revolver were drawn to fund further insider buybacks. The Board has also had a leadership advisory firm assisting with long-term succession planning since July 2025, which lowers the risk that the end-2026 transition is unplanned. A single Class B voting block can also be an asset to creditors if it is a stable, long-horizon holder, which the sources neither confirm nor rule out.
### Limitations

- The board, executive officers, compensation and beneficial ownership tables are in a proxy statement or annual report amendment that was not supplied, so the conclusion on board independence is not established and the conclusion on control rests on the notes and risk factors only.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 264

- No successor to the chief executive is named in the sources and the succession process is described only in general terms, so the conclusion on leadership continuity cannot be taken beyond 2026-12-31.

- The price paid in the repurchases from the chief executive is stated only as the closing price on the transaction date, so the cash cost of the insider repurchases is not established and the conclusion that capital returns are tilted toward insiders rests on share counts.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 70–71

- Fee flows with Cantor affiliates are stated for administrative services, servicing for Cantor Commercial Real Estate, one referral fee and the notes underwriting fee, and otherwise only as authorization limits, so the scale of related-party fee income and expense beyond those items is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 80–81

- Ownership diagrams are carried as text only, so indirect holdings below Cantor and CFGM are taken from the stated percentages and the conclusion on economic interest excludes anything the diagram would show.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 134

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The parent's only public debt issue is the 7.500% senior notes due 2029, issued on 2024-01-12 for USD 600.0 million as general senior unsecured obligations; Cantor bought USD 125.0 million, which is 20.83% of the issue, and still holds it. The revolving credit facility was amended and restated on 2026-04-17, raising it to USD 900.0 million with a maturity of 2030-04-17 and a right to increase to USD 1.1 billion. A repurchase agreement for the Multifamily Bridge Program with a USD 300.0 million facility amount was signed on 2026-08-27, and USD 28.0 million was borrowed under it at 2026-09-30, carried inside other liabilities.

No sponsor transaction, merger or change of control is stated in the sources. Control changed within the family when Mr. Howard Lutnick completed the divestiture of his holdings on 2025-10-06, and four small cash acquisitions were completed in 2026 for USD 34.6 million in total.

# Fundamental credit for Newmark Group, Inc.
## Request

Fundamental credit for Newmark Group, Inc. (issuer nmrk-1690680), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: an integrated credit view from the 2025 annual report, the third-quarter 2026 quarterly report and earnings release, and the three earlier modules; no executed debt document, proxy statement, peer or market data is in scope.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Newmark's fundamental credit profile is average: moderate leverage, strong liquidity and fee revenue spread across service lines support debt service, but capital returns above free cash flow, a lowered outlook and controlling-holder influence leave little room above the lowest investment-grade ratings.

Net debt is 1.38x reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, or 1.41x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-10-28, cash interest cover is 8.17x, and undrawn revolver capacity is USD 620 million with no corporate maturity before 2029. Against that, shareholder returns were 1.39x free cash flow excluding loan activity in the nine months, capital markets revenue fell 4.36% in the third quarter, and management lowered its 2026 outlook.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 116; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C8; calculation C33; calculation C30; calculation C9
### Key findings

Leverage is moderate but has risen, and the measure matters. Net debt to reported EBITDA moved from 1.07x at FY2025 to 1.38x at 2026-09-30, or 1.41x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-10-28, against 1.40x at FY2024, while last-twelve-month reported EBITDA grew 10.84%; on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA the ratio is 1.00x, and total debt to reported EBITDA is 1.91x. The revolver draw rose alongside capital returns and investment, so leverage is a policy outcome rather than a result of falling earnings.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C31

Liquidity and the maturity profile are the main support for the credit. Undrawn revolver capacity is USD 620 million, no corporate debt matures before 2029 and the revolver runs to 2030. The filings state covenant compliance but print no debt covenant level; the one capital test with a printed margin is Fannie Mae's net worth requirement, where the margin was USD 351.0 million at 2026-09-30, down from USD 386.7 million at year-end 2025, so the headroom that would make the liquidity usable under stress is established for that test alone.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 112; calculation C8; calculation C33; calculation C44

Market access is adequate but sits at the lowest investment-grade step. Fitch and S&P both rate the company BBB- with stable outlooks, S&P having raised its rating from BB+ on 2026-09-16, and the quarterly report says the rate on the senior notes due 2029 may rise by up to 2% after a downgrade; at that maximum the extra interest is USD 12.00 million a year and cover falls from 8.17x to 6.73x.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 116; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C42; calculation C43; calculation C5

Revenue is diversified and about two-fifths recurring, but the transaction lines are slowing at the margin and management has lowered its outlook. Management services and servicing are 39.57% of nine-month revenue and grew 18.30% in the third quarter, and leasing grew 26.49%, but capital markets revenue fell 4.36% in the quarter although it is still 14.55% higher over the nine months, while the ten-year Treasury yield rose about 113 bp in the quarter to 5.3%; the midpoint of the 2026 revenue outlook was cut by 1.96% and that of the adjusted EBITDA outlook by 4.00% because the timing of deal closings is uncertain.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 96–97; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 8; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11; calculation C10; calculation C9; calculation C39; calculation C23; calculation C35; calculation C14; calculation C15

Margins look resilient because much of the cost base is variable. Compensation and employee benefits are 59.12% of FY2025 revenue and producers earn a substantial portion or all of their pay from production, so costs fall with commissions; the last-twelve-month reported EBITDA margin is 12.39% against 12.32% at FY2024, and the issuer's adjusted margin is 17.25%. Depreciation, lease costs and cash interest do not flex, so a sustained fall in deal volume would compress margin faster than revenue.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C20; calculation C28; calculation C29

Financial policy is the weakest dimension: capital returns are running ahead of free cash flow and are tilted toward insiders. Shareholder returns were 1.39x free cash flow excluding loan activity in the nine months against 1.34x a year earlier, so the gap is persistent and not new, net revolver borrowing was 0.97x of share repurchases, 98.48% of third-quarter repurchases came from the chief executive and his foundation, and the quarterly dividend doubled to USD 0.06 per share, so creditors are competing with equity for cash while the revolver is drawn.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C18; calculation C30; calculation C62; calculation C63; calculation C19; calculation C48; calculation C25; calculation C36

Governance adds risk beyond the numbers. Mr. Brandon Lutnick controls 58.6% of the vote through Cantor and CFGM, Cantor holds 20.83% of the senior notes, the chief executive is contracted as chief executive only through 2026-12-31 with no successor named, and the company is a controlled company that could drop board independence requirements, though it has not done so; the Audit Committee is the stated check on related-party dealing.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C37; calculation C24

The lending business adds claims outside corporate debt that the headline leverage omits. Warehouse facilities fund 99.02% of loans held for sale and are recourse only to a subsidiary, so they are excluded from corporate debt, but total debt including them is 2.49x the corporate figure; separately, Newmark shares losses on Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac loans, with a stated maximum potential loss of about USD 12.1 billion against a risk-sharing liability equal to 0.29% of it, so the exposure is small on expected loss and very large on a maximum basis.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a better view is momentum, modest leverage and improving ratings: nine-month revenue grew 18.36%, third-quarter revenue grew 12.71%, last-twelve-month reported EBITDA is 10.84% above FY2025, net leverage on the issuer's own adjusted measure is 1.00x, S&P raised the rating to BBB- on 2026-09-16, and management still expects its best-ever full year. The profile would improve if shareholder returns fell back inside free cash flow and the revolver were repaid, if a chief executive successor were named with an orderly handover, and if the executed credit agreement showed ample covenant headroom. It would weaken if capital markets revenue fell again year on year in the fourth quarter, if net leverage stayed above the FY2024 level of 1.40x after the dividend, if revolver availability fell toward the USD 365 million of 2026-03-31, or if a downgrade triggered the rate increase on the notes.

### Strengths and weaknesses

Newmark is an average credit with a stable bias: its strengths are balance-sheet and revenue-mix qualities that protect debt service, and its weaknesses are choices by owners and management and a deal market that has turned less supportive.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C8

Liquidity is the first strength: USD 620 million of undrawn revolver, a first corporate maturity in 2029 and BBB- ratings at Fitch and S&P mean refinancing is not a near-term pressure, so stress would show in leverage and ratings before it shows in cash. Moderate leverage is the second: 1.38x on reported EBITDA and cover of 8.17x leave room to absorb a weaker year. Recurring management and servicing revenue, 39.57% of nine-month revenue, is the third because it does not depend on deal closings. A largely commission-based cost base is the fourth because compensation moves with revenue and limits margin loss when deals slow. Earnings momentum is the fifth: last-twelve-month reported EBITDA is 10.84% above FY2025.

Dependence on deal volumes is the third: capital markets revenue fell 4.36% in the third quarter and management lowered its outlook. ### Business model, ownership and revenue durability

Newmark is a commercial real estate adviser and service provider with three revenue lines: management services, servicing fees and other; leasing and other commissions; and capital markets. About two-fifths of nine-month revenue is recurring fee income and the top ten clients were 9.1% of FY2025 revenue, so debt service does not rest on one client or one line. The cost of that breadth is dependence on the transaction lines, which follow deal volumes and interest rates, so cash-flow visibility is good for the fee half of the business and weak for the commission half.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C23; calculation C38; calculation C11; calculation C10; calculation C9

One holder controls the vote: Mr. Brandon Lutnick controls 58.6% of it through Cantor and CFGM, Cantor holds 20.83% of the senior notes, and related-party services, lending and note placement run through the same group. Control is stable rather than contestable, which lowers takeover risk but means borrowing, distributions and board makeup follow one group's preferences, and creditor protection rests on Audit Committee approval of related-party matters. No sponsor transaction, merger or change of control is stated in the documents.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C37; calculation C24

Revenue is cyclical in its transaction half and sticky in its fee half. Leasing grew 26.49% and management services and servicing grew 18.30% in the third quarter, while capital markets fell 4.36% although it is still 14.55% higher over the nine months, so the commission lines now pull in different directions. Management states a goal of more than USD 2 billion of annual management and servicing revenue by 2029; that is management language, not a forecast, and it would raise the recurring share only if met.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C11; calculation C10; calculation C9; calculation C39; calculation C49
### Cost structure and cash conversion

Cost flexibility is good where it matters. Compensation and employee benefits are 59.12% of FY2025 revenue and follow commission-based revenue, as the third-quarter release attributes the cost increase primarily to higher commission-based revenue, acquired companies and growth investment, so a drop in deal fees is partly met by lower pay. Depreciation, lease costs and cash interest do not flex, and the last-twelve-month reported EBITDA margin of 12.39% is close to the 12.32% of FY2024 even though the adjusted margin is 17.25%, because the reported measure carries equity-based compensation as a cost.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C20; calculation C28; calculation C29

Cash conversion is high and capital intensity low. Free cash flow excluding loan activity was 72.52% of last-twelve-month reported EBITDA against 57.59% in FY2024, after cash interest and taxes, and purchases of fixed assets are 1.53% of last-twelve-month revenue, so little cash is locked in maintenance spending and capital spending is easy to cut. The main recurring use of operating cash is advances to employees and partners to hire and retain producers; loan originations swing reported operating cash flow but are matched by warehouse funding, so the swing is timing and not a drain on corporate cash.

### Market forces and external factors

Competitive rivalry is the force that matters most to margins and market position. The annual report describes an industry that is fragmented and competitive, names larger rivals such as CBRE, Jones Lang LaSalle and Cushman & Wakefield, and says some competitors are substantially larger than Newmark; the third-quarter report says Newmark believes it gained share in investment sales, yet its U.S. debt volumes fell about 37% while industry originations rose, which the issuer ties to a strong prior-year comparison. Buyer power is limited by client spread, with the top ten clients at 9.1% of FY2025 revenue and clients increasingly awarding work to full-service firms. Supplier power sits with producers, who earn a substantial portion or all of their pay from production and are retained with advances, so producer departures are a margin and revenue risk. The documents do not discuss new entrants or substitutes, so those forces are not established.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 97; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C38; calculation C40

The external factors that move credit are economic and regulatory. A ten-year Treasury yield up about 113 bp in the quarter to 5.3%, tied by the issuer to the Middle East conflict and energy prices, raises financing costs and rate volatility for property buyers and offsets the help from narrow credit spreads. Agency programs add a regulatory layer: capital and liquidity requirements for Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac lending include the net worth test the issuer calls its most restrictive, and the Fannie Mae loss-sharing exposure rises with agency loan performance. Technology cuts both ways, because artificial intelligence firms drive office leasing demand while the annual report lists their use as a risk.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

The next one to two years turn on the fourth quarter and on the rate path. The revised outlook implies fourth-quarter revenue growth of between -1.40% and 8.54% against the fourth quarter of 2025, with 3.57% at the midpoint, compared with 12.71% in the third quarter, and the fourth quarter has averaged about 30% of annual revenue, so the outlook leaves little cushion if closings slip. Tailwinds are the leasing recovery led by technology demand, growth in servicing fees and the refinancing wave in industry mortgage maturities; headwinds are rate volatility, the issuer's U.S. debt volumes falling about 37% in the third quarter against a strong prior-year comparison, and lower guidance.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 97; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 98; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_nmrk-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C54; calculation C56; calculation C55; calculation C57; calculation C12; calculation C50; calculation C40; calculation C41

Over three to five years the question is refinancing. The senior notes due 2029 of USD 600.0 million become current in 2028, the revolver matures in 2030, and the notes carry a rate that rises on a downgrade, so keeping the investment-grade ratings matters more than any single quarter. Management's goal of more than USD 2 billion of recurring management and servicing revenue by 2029 would improve visibility if met, but it is management language and carries no stated probability.

### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is long-term rates that stay near 5.3% through the year-end selling season, so closings slip and the fourth quarter lands at the low end of the revised outlook, which implies fourth-quarter revenue growth of -1.40%. The first operational break is in the transaction lines, leasing and capital markets, while servicing and management fees keep growing. Compensation flexes with commissions, but depreciation, lease costs and cash interest do not, so reported EBITDA falls faster than revenue. As a severity marker chosen by the analyst, not a forecast, take reported EBITDA back at its FY2024 level: net debt at 2026-09-30 would then be 1.89x EBITDA, or 1.92x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-10-28, and interest cover would be 5.98x.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nmrk-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 96; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_nmrkex991secversion.htm.jsonl, page 8; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C56; calculation C58; calculation C59; calculation C60

Liquidity holds in this case. USD 620 million of the revolver is undrawn and no corporate debt matures before 2029, so no refinancing event arises within the scenario. Management has levers: share repurchases and the dividend are discretionary with USD 189.5 million of repurchase authorization still unused, purchases of fixed assets are only 1.53% of revenue, and producer pay flexes. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress; the first constraint would be leverage at 1.89x to 1.92x and the investment-grade ratings, where a downgrade lifts the notes rate, and not cash. The scenario would break this view only if repurchases continued at the nine-month pace while earnings fell.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C8; calculation C33; calculation C53; calculation C61; calculation C42
### Overall credit view

Overall, Newmark presents an adequate business profile supported by revenue spread across three service lines, low capital intensity and investment-grade ratings at Fitch and S&P, but credit quality is constrained by capital returns above free cash flow, controlling-holder influence and an earnings base that depends on deal closings in the fourth quarter. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow excluding loan activity converted 72.52% of last-twelve-month reported EBITDA and about two-fifths of revenue is recurring. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on keeping the BBB- ratings and on the notes due 2029 being refinanced before they become current. The primary downside path is a weak fourth quarter and a downgrade while the revolver funds distributions. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indenture, the proxy statement, and peer and market data. Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: shareholder returns funded by the revolver ahead of a deal-dependent fourth quarter.
